## Plan

### Mechanics summary
- 379 HP `[GAME-EXTRACT]`. Opening cycle: Curse of Knowledge → Slap 17 → Knowledge Overwhelming 8×3 → Ponder (11 damage, heals, +2 Strength) `[GAME-EXTRACT]`.
- **Curse of Knowledge** `[COMMUNITY]`: choose one of two status cards each time, for three cycles. A second guide (selphie1999gaming, 2026-03-24, accessed 2026-11-19) gives the pairs: **Disintegration or Mind Rot, then Disintegration or Sloth, then Disintegration or Waste Away**. The four cards exist in the game data with these effects `[GAME-EXTRACT]` (corroborates the guides; Sloth corrected):
  - **Disintegration:** a power that deals 6 damage to you at the end of each turn (the guides: 6, 7, then 8 in later offers). It is a Counter power, so taking it twice adds the amounts (6 + 7 = 13 a turn) `[GAME-EXTRACT]`
  - **Mind Rot:** draw 1 fewer card each turn
  - **Sloth:** you can play **at most 3 cards per turn** (the guide said "draw at most 3"; the power checks cards played)
  - **Waste Away:** 1 less max energy
  - **Choice rule** `[HYPOTHESIS]` model: **offer 1 Mind Rot, offer 2 Sloth; offer 3 is close** (Waste Away slightly ahead; Disintegration is fine when the fight ends within about 2 turns). A simulation of all eight combinations (`reports/phase2/vantom-simulation.md`, 22-card deck from full HP) puts Disintegration at offer 1 or 2 far behind, because its damage stacks for the rest of the fight: offer 1 Mind Rot 35% against Disintegration 5%, offer 2 Sloth 35% against 16%, offer 3 Waste Away 35% against 31% (the model is pessimistic in absolute terms; it fails calibration for this boss). The earlier ranking (always Sloth > Mind Rot > Waste Away > Disintegration) assumed any card could be taken at any offer, which the guides contradict.
- **The wiki confirms the modelled fight** `[COMMUNITY]` (slaythespire.wiki.gg page, accessed 2026-11-19): HP 379 (399 at A8+); Slap 17, Knowledge Overwhelming 8×3, Ponder 11 + heal 30 per player + 2 Strength (13, +3 at A9); the three curse offers and their numbers as above; curse cards are played at once and removed from the game.
- **Model calibration** `[HYPOTHESIS]` model: with the best curse plan the 22-card model deck wins 18% from 60/80 against the Player's 8/12. No single mechanic change closes the gap (heal 15: 19%, no heal 21%, Ponder without Strength 28%, Overwhelming 8×2 31%), and simulated fights last 10 turns against the Player's 7, so the shortfall is mostly deck strength (no relics, upgrades or many card effects in the model), not the cycle.
- After three cycles, a plain Slap / Overwhelming / Ponder loop. Ponder heals 30 per player `[COMMUNITY]`, two guides; the game data shows the heal as computed (`Heal ? HP`).

### Deck checklist
- **Countable checks** (`tools/deck_check.py`, tuned on the history 2026-11-19) `[PLAYER-DATA, weak]`: Strength cards at least 1 (survived 0.7, fatal 0.2 (H7)); energy cards at least 1 (survived 1.6, fatal 0.8 (H7)).
- **Sustained damage.** 379 HP plus about 30 healed per cycle over a median 7-turn fight means about 60 damage per turn. Ironclad gets this from scaling (Demon Form; Strength with multi-hit) and energy (Pyre, Bloodletting, Offering).
- In the history, fatal decks had fewer powers (1.7 against 2.7), fewer energy cards (0.8 against 1.6) and less Strength (0.2 against 0.7), n=40. `[PLAYER-DATA, weak]`
- **Block** for Overwhelming (24 base, rising with Strength) and Slap (17).

### Curse choice `[HYPOTHESIS]`
- Offer 1 (Disintegration or Mind Rot): **Mind Rot**.
- Offer 2 (Disintegration or Sloth): **Sloth**, unless the deck plays many 0-cost cards (Sloth caps cards played at 3).
- Offer 3 (Disintegration or Waste Away): close. **Waste Away** by default; **Disintegration** when the fight will end within about 2 turns or the deck needs every energy (X-cost cards, 3-cost cards).
- Never stack Disintegration: the second one makes it 13 a turn.

### HP target on arrival
- Ironclad benchmark: median 45, p75 59.8. **Rest before the boss if HP is below about 55.**

### First three turns
1. Set up: powers first (Demon Form, Pyre). Take the curse choice above.
2. Slap 17: block, keep scaling.
3. Overwhelming 8×3: block. Weak on the boss makes each hit 6.
4. Ponder: no big attack, so deal maximum damage. Every Ponder heals, so the fight has to end quickly.

### Potion plan
- Strength, Flex and energy potions early, so scaling starts sooner.
- Block potion for Overwhelming.
- Keep one damage potion to finish without letting it Ponder again.

### What killed the Player here, and the counter
- Ironclad: 4 of 12 fatal, median 45 damage (all characters: 13 of 40 fatal, median 38). Arrival HP was similar in fatal and survived fights (67% against 72%). The damage race was lost (fatal fights took a median 53 damage). `[PLAYER-DATA]`
- Counter: arrive with a scaling engine. Act 2 drafting should prioritise powers and energy once the boss is known.

### The Agent's fights here (2026-11-23)
- **Record** `[OBS]` (A0, simulator on v0.111.1, the runs' fight search): 6 of 17 fights won (10 seeds, two arms; HP 70% at the start, 26.6 cards, 7.9 relics) in run benchmark 17 against 29 of 42 in run benchmark 16, with the same search and about the same state at the fight's start (`reports/phase9/run-bench-17.md` section 5). Other seeds, and a seed fixes its boss, so the two figures are a description and no test. The trace of a lost fight here is owed by decision 0006 and has not been read yet.

### The Agent's fights here, traced (2026-11-23)
- **The curse was never chosen: the fight search took the first option at every card choice, and the first option is Disintegration.** `[OBS]` 59 fights replayed from the situations of run benchmarks 16 and 17 with every decision kept (`reports/phase9/boss-replay-3.md` and `run-bench-17.md`, section 6): Disintegration at all 59 first offers, all 52 second offers and all 4 third offers. The plan above ranks it last at the first two offers; with two taken the player loses 13 HP at the end of every turn after the second offer. Lost fights ended on turn 6 in 16 of 29.
- **The fights the Agent won were races that ended first.** `[OBS]` run benchmark 17's 17 situations: fights won dealt 63 damage a turn (median) and ended on turn 6 or 7 in 6 of 7; fights lost dealt 39 a turn. HP on arrival 75% of the maximum in the fights won, 60% in the fights lost.
- **Whether choosing the curse wins more of these fights is under test** (boss replay 4, `reports/phase9/boss-replay-4.md`: the answers to a card choice searched like any other action). Until it is read, the choice rule above stays a hypothesis.
